title: Learning to read music with Manuel Perez
summary: Williams took him to Manuel Perez (and Puri) to learn reading; by 1933 he was ready for his first big job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: self-conscious about it? It was later on that Alfred Williams said, well, George says, told my mother, say, this youngster's playing a hell of a lot of horn and he don't know how to read. So we better, I better take him to a guy who will teach him how to read. So he brought me to Manuel Perez. There was a Manuel Puri and a Manuel Perez. Well, I went to both of them and Manuel Perez was the one that taught me how to read between those two.
How do you spell his name?
P-O-R-E-E, Puri, and the other one is P-E-R-E-Z.
Yeah, but you studied with both of them. The one who taught you how to read was... Yeah.
So I took a few lessons and the rest of it I figured it out for myself.

And so that was about 1930, 31 I started and, you know, about 31 I started reading and 33 I had it pretty well done. You did? Yeah. Yeah. Well, I went on the Steamer Captain by that time. That was my first big job.
